titles: “IT'S NOT GOING TO HAPPEN!” Arman Tsarukyan SHUTS DOWN Topuria As Ilia Returns To Training!
“HE IS ONE OF THE BEST IN THE WORLD!” Justin Gaethje On Ilia Topuria's Comeback!
“NO CHANCE!” Chael Sonnen SHUTS DOWN Ilia Topuria Featherweight Return!
“PADDY'S A PROBLEM!” Justin Gaethje BREAKS DOWN Topuria vs Pimblett!

blocks.narration: Ilia Topuria is back in the gym. After the first loss of his career, against Justin Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 in June, he has shared new training footage, and the lightweight division is already split on what comes next. Even the man who beat him says Topuria is still one of the best in the world.

Meanwhile, Justin Gaethje explains what he thinks separated him from Ilia Topuria at UFC Freedom 250 in June 2026. He points to mindset, experience, Trevor Wittman’s game plan, and where he believed Topuria was mentally before the fight.

On the other side, Justin Gaethje highlights how dangerous Ilia Topuria still looked before they fought at the White House. He says Topuria’s knockouts over Charles Oliveira and Max Holloway forced him to train with urgency every day.

At the same time, Justin Gaethje weighs in on whether Topuria truly belongs at lightweight after moving up as a two-division UFC champion. He defends Topuria’s skill level, but he also questions how long that size equation can hold at 155.
Chael Sonnen is just as clear about where Topuria goes from here. Asked whether Topuria could drop back to featherweight, his answer is an emphatic no.
Sonnen explains why: in his view, Topuria stays at 155 until he solves the problem there, and would only consider 145 after winning the lightweight belt back.

At the same time, Chael Sonnen agrees with Sean O’Malley’s read on why Topuria lost to Justin Gaethje. Sonnen says inactivity and major life changes mattered because Topuria had not competed for a year before that five-round challenge.
Arman Tsarukyan does not count Topuria out after the first loss of his career. He says the setback could make Topuria more motivated, more hungry, and more locked in when he returns.

Arman Tsarukyan, the No. 1 contender, says the UFC gave him the same message before and after his knockout of Mauricio Ruffy at UFC 331. According to Arman, the promotion is working on his title fight next.

On the other side, Arman Tsarukyan lays out why he thinks Gaethje would prefer Ilia Topuria over him. He says Gaethje has already beaten Topuria once, while Arman represents a different challenge at the top of lightweight.
Arman Tsarukyan also expects Topuria's team to push for a title shot first. He says it will not happen, and predicts Topuria fights Paddy Pimblett instead.

Beyond that, Justin Gaethje reveals the other complication around the lightweight belt right now. He says he is hurt, cannot fight again this year, and expects the next conversation about his future closer to Christmas.

Adding to that, Jon Anik admits the champion’s future may be more uncertain than the division wants to hear. He discusses Gaethje’s legacy through violence and memorable moments, then leaves open the possibility that the Topuria win could be the last one.

Taking that further, Jon Anik questions what the UFC actually does if Justin Gaethje is willing to continue. He says the promotion likely makes the Arman Tsarukyan fight, while also noting how strongly the betting market already leans.

However, Jon Anik also keeps the Ilia Topuria rematch in the conversation because of Topuria’s profile. He says the UFC has to consider that option internally, even while acknowledging that Tsarukyan’s latest win makes him deserving.

Taking that further, Jon Anik says Arman Tsarukyan has now become extremely hard to ignore for the next lightweight title shot. He still gives Justin Gaethje a legitimate chance, but frames Arman as promotionally undeniable after the Ruffy knockout.

Before UFC 331, Chael Sonnen had already made the case for Topuria. He says that with Topuria's credentials as a two-division champion, it is hard to argue he does not deserve to fight for the belt he just held.

However, Paddy Pimblett remains the other major name attached to Ilia Topuria’s comeback. Justin Gaethje weighs in on that matchup and says Paddy becomes difficult to beat when an opponent gives him space to work.

Then, Justin Gaethje keeps the Paddy Pimblett fight alive because of the matchup and the history between Paddy and Topuria. He says Paddy is a real problem, and the trash talk makes that pairing even more interesting.

On a similar note, Arman Tsarukyan gives his own read on Ilia Topuria versus Paddy Pimblett. He calls it a close fight because Paddy’s chin and cardio could make Topuria’s knockout path harder than expected.

outro: Gaethje has the belt and the leverage, Tsarukyan has the contender case, and Topuria is back training with Paddy still circling. What happens next could reshape the division. So, drop your thoughts below.
description:
Ilia Topuria is back in training after his first professional loss, and the UFC lightweight division is already moving around him. Justin Gaethje is champion, Arman Tsarukyan says he is next, and Paddy Pimblett continues to call for the Topuria fight.

This episode looks at the comeback options: an immediate Gaethje rematch, a Paddy Pimblett grudge fight, or a more gradual return while Gaethje and Arman sort out the title picture.

Credits: The Ariel Helwani Show, DOUBLE COVERAGE PODCAST, Submission Radio, Chael Sonnen.
pinned_comment: Who should Ilia Topuria fight next: Paddy Pimblett, a gradual comeback opponent, or Justin Gaethje in the rematch?
